data.title: Z80 REPL (2018)
data.author: adunk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Z80 汇编 REPL 的实用性、交互体验及功能扩展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 怀旧与历史对比：flyinghamster 回忆 Apple II 的 Monitor，认为其 Mini-Assembler 曾是接近“汇编语言 REPL”的工具，但 Apple II Plus 为加入自动启动功能而移除了它，只保留了反汇编器。  
• 肯定项目创意但关注维护状况：jottinger 指出该项目源代码似乎已有 8 年历史，同时仍认为“在 REPL 中进行汇编”的想法很棒。  
• 功能增强派：jhallenworld 建议支持符号、标签和前向引用解析，并以 6800/6809 Exorciser 模拟器为例，展示 `start`、`skip`、`loop` 等标签及偏移修正信息；还希望输入 `a` 后进入内置编辑器，退出时自动汇编。  
• 交互体验改进：networked 发现无操作数指令后输入尾随空格会导致解析错误，例如 `nop ` 被识别为未知指令；同时建议支持类似 fish 的 Tab 循环选择补全项。  
• 即时反馈的价值：torutofu 认为 REPL 能让用户快速恢复 Z80 汇编的熟练度。  
• 教学与示例需求：j4cobgarby 希望提供可直接加载进内存的示例程序。

补充讨论：整体态度积极，争议主要不在项目价值，而在功能成熟度与易用性：符号/编辑器等高级功能、空白处理和补全机制，决定其能否从有趣的实验工具发展为高效的开发环境。

data.title: Tokens too cheap to meter
data.author: teoruiz
data.article_summary: 文章指出，机器学习智能的使用成本正以每年数个数量级下降，主要受GPU效率提升、模型能力增强与推理引擎优化推动。未来一两年，LLM将像基础设施一样融入各类计算；未来3—6年，前沿水平模型可能在普通硬件本地运行。届时AI应用瓶颈将从算力和令牌数量转向质量、可及性及实际需求，并引发供需两侧的“杰文斯悖论”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI 推理与完成特定任务的成本快速下降，是否会持续，以及这对商业模式、硬件厂商和技术应用意味着什么。

不同观点：
• 乐观观点：Epoch AI 数据显示，达到同等性能的成本仍在快速下降；推测解码等技术可用一次前向计算生成多个 token，可能进一步降低推理成本。若市场保持竞争，推理将逐渐商品化。
• 谨慎观点：成本下降不可能永远保持指数速度，最终可能接近高效软件工具（如 grep）的成本下限，而非持续超越。有人还指出文章混淆了“完整智能指数成本”和“单任务加权平均成本”，夸大了降价幅度。
• 商业模式质疑：基础设施投资已达数万亿美元，但文章缺少盈利能力分析。若资本规模达一万亿美元，年回报率超过10%就需要持续创造至少千亿美元自由现金流，未来如何实现尚不清楚。
• 硬件观点：NVIDIA 在训练领域仍有优势，但推理市场竞争更激烈、利润可能下降；VRAM、统一内存和晶圆产能将决定本地模型普及速度。
• 数据与图表批评：部分评论认为趋势线缺少噪声检验，GPU 图表难以支持文章结论，甚至显示 H100 与新硬件效率差距有限。Artificial Analysis 的“最具吸引力象限”也被批评为缺乏决策意义。

补充讨论：有人将“AI 便宜到可忽略”类比核能“便宜到无需计量”的历史预言，提醒技术乐观叙事可能高估现实；另有观点主张能不用 AI 就不用，并质疑其网络安全宣传。

49813482.article_content:
Table of contents
Is this really happening?
Improvements that affect all AI
Improvements that affect hosted AI
Improvements that affect local AI
Improvements that affect specialized use cases
Putting it together
What happens next?
Tokens become cheaper than tool calls
Supply-side Jevons Paradox
How are investors going to make their money back?
Demand-side Jevons Paradox
Optionality
Summary
The price of using machine learning intelligence is decreasing by several orders of magnitude a year and shows no signs of slowing.
We are likely to see LLMs integrated into every part of computing as infrastructure, not just as a product, in the next year or two.
We are likely to see LLMs running locally at current frontier-quality on commodity hardware in the next 3-6 years.
Starting very soon, we are likely to see
quality
and
access
become the limiting factor to AI
1
use, not sheer number of tokens.
Is this really happening?
Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, so I collected a whole bunch of evidence.
AI can be either proprietary (such as GPT-6 Astra) or open weight (such as GLM-5.3-flash).
Open weight models can be either hosted (e.g. by Z.ai) or local.
Generally, models intended to be run locally will be much smaller, such as
Muse Glimmer
or
Qwen3 Coder
.
Improvements in one don't always affect improvements in the others.
Improvements that affect all AI
GPUs
GPUs are getting exponentially more efficient with every generation.
In the graph below (
source
), the X-axis is time and the Y-axis is power efficiency of the GPU itself.
Larger Y-axis numbers mean more efficient.
This is a logarithmic graph, which is to say that a straight line on the graph represents an exponential increase in efficiency.
In this particular case, the logarithm is 1.3, which means efficiency doubles about once every two years.
This is an increase in efficiency that we haven't seen since Moore's Law in the 1960s.
Models
The cost to complete a given task with a model is going down sharply over time.
Models are usually priced per-token.
A "token" is a fragment of a word; it takes about 1.5 tokens to represent a word.
For every token a model reads, and for every token it outputs, the "model provider" (e.g. Anthropic or OpenAI) charges you some fixed amount of money.
The cost per
token
of models is not consistently going down, at least not for the smartest ("frontier") models.
But the cost per
task
is.
Smaller models may cost less per token, but use more tokens overall than a larger model for the same task, because they have to think more or correct their first drafts.
This section is about the cost to complete the task from beginning to end.
The chart below (
source
) shows the "
pareto frontier
" of cost/task at present.
A pareto frontier shows the best
tradeoff
you can get, not just the best in a single category.
Here, our tradeoffs are:
Y-axis: the "quality" of the model (as measured by a suite of benchmarks)
X-axis: the cost to complete those benchmarks
Cost is on a logarithmic scale.
Larger Y-axis and smaller X-axis numbers are better.
This is showing us a wide range of models on the pareto frontier as of 2026.
Towards the top-right we have Claude Fable-5.1 (expensive and intelligent); towards the middle-left we have GPT-5.6 Luna (cheap and less intelligent).
Models below the dotted line are basically not worth considering.
2
Now, look at this chart showing the frontier at the start, middle, and end of
2025
:
The chart shows models are getting smarter
and
cheaper on a per-task basis over 2025.
If you draw a straight horizontal line at basically any task on the Y-axis, the cost to do it at the end of 2025 was cheaper than at the start;
and if you draw a straight vertical line at basically any point on the X-axis, models can do more for the same cost.
Now, compare that 2025 chart to the 2026 chart.
The Y-axis (intelligence) is about the same, with less of a fall-off towards the cheap end.
The X-axis (cost) has gotten
two orders of magnitude cheaper
.
Inference Engines
An "inference engine" is a software package that takes a trained model and an input text and actually runs it on a GPU.
Inference engines are currently immature and improving rapidly.
Currently we're seeing 10%-50% improvements year-over-year, depending on which engine you look at.
There are two benchmarks that are often compared for inference engines:
"offline" (run a bunch of tokens through in one big batch)
and "serving" (you have people sending your server inputs at unpredictable times, and you want to send a response back as quickly as possible).
Serving is getting efficient much more rapidly than offline inference.
All numbers below are for serving workloads, not offline.
vLLM
vLLM
is an open-source inference engine and it's getting more efficient over time.
In the graph below (
source
), the Y-axis is Joules/token, the X-axis is batch size (roughly: "how many inputs are processed in parallel?"), and the blue/red lines are different software versions.
Smalle

data.title: ArXiv receives multiyear commitments to support it as an independent nonprofit
data.author: JohnHammersley
data.article_summary: arXiv宣布获西蒙斯基金会国际、XTX Markets和Siegel家庭基金会共计1720万美元的多年期资助，支持其转型为独立非营利组织。资金将用于平台运营与技术升级、应对人工智能生成内容等学术传播挑战，并加强治理和组织建设，以持续为全球科研人员提供开放、可靠的科研交流服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ArXiv在开放获取与科研信息传播中的价值，以及AI生成、低质量或伪装成研究的内容对其可信度的冲击。

不同观点：
• 批评内容泛滥：AI生成论文大量涌入，审核难以及时跟上；部分作者借ArXiv包装宣传或观点文章，利用其科学平台形象获取可信度。有人因此对2023年后的单人投稿、尤其是无研究机构背景的作者持怀疑态度，但也承认并非所有独立研究者都不可靠。  
• 维护开放价值：ArXiv让研究成果免费获取，避免付费墙阻碍科学发展；企业研究者认为，即使没有ArXiv，他们的成果可能只能以博客形式出现，缺乏可引用性。  
• 对替代机制也不乐观：OpenReview虽有同行评审功能，但评论者可能使用LLM，或根本没有认真阅读，说明问题不只是ArXiv审核不足，而是评审质量整体受影响。  
• 保留但降低信任：有人认可ArXiv曾是有价值的资源，但过去就存在为晋升、签证等目的发布的低质量论文，因此平台的可信度早已受到损害。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于如何在开放发布、快速传播与质量控制之间取得平衡；AI既依赖ArXiv训练，又可能反过来污染其内容生态。

49823664.article_content:
arXiv receives Multiyear Philanthropic Commitments to Support Its Launch as an Independent Nonprofit
By Kat Boboris
·
September 23
rd
2026
arXiv is pleased to announce that three leading philanthropic organizations have provided multimillion-dollar support for arXiv. These new multiyear philanthropic commitments from
Simons Foundation International, XTX Markets, and Siegel Family Endowment
will support platform development, organizational capacity, and overall provide foundational support to arXiv’s establishment as an independent nonprofit. The $17.2 million investment, spanning three to five years, will support arXiv as it transitions to independence by strengthening its technical infrastructure, supporting ongoing operations, and improving services for researchers around the world.
For three and a half decades, arXiv has been a trusted venue where researchers can share and access scientific findings. Today, we serve millions of users annually and play an essential role in scholarly communication across physics, mathematics, computer science, quantitative biology, quantitative finance, statistics, electrical engineering and systems science, and economics.
Helping Fund a New Organization
I am grateful for the commitments from Simons Foundation International, XTX Markets, and Siegel Family Endowment, which put arXiv on solid footing as we move into this next chapter. Their generous support provides a strong foundation and momentum for arXiv to continue to grow and serve the research community for the long term.” The new commitments build on previous philanthropic support for arXiv. arXiv gratefully acknowledges their community-based donors, including member organizations, foundations, affiliates, sponsors, and longstanding supporters.
penelope lewis, chief executive officer, arxiv
These new commitments will support three core areas of work:
General operation and ongoing improvement of arXiv’s services for the research community;
Continued technical development of the platform, including work related to the management of AI-generated content and other emerging challenges in scholarly communication; and
Strengthening of arXiv as an independent nonprofit, including investments in governance and organizational operations.
Simons Foundation International
Building on the Simons Foundation’s long-standing support of arXiv, Simons Foundation International has made a new multi-year commitment to support the organization’s next phase as an independent nonprofit.
For 35 years, arXiv has made math and science more open, transparent, accessible and collaborative. By growing into an independent nonprofit, arXiv will be positioned to evolve and modernize its systems to better serve the scientific community and to secure its future.
david spergel, president, simons foundation
XTX Markets
XTX Markets and its founder, Alex Gerko, have supported arXiv’s mission for the past two years. The firm is now making a new multi-year commitment to strengthen arXiv’s role as a trusted platform for open scientific research.
For decades, arXiv has been an important bedrock for open science. Now, with rapid advances in AI driving changes across academia, it is even more valuable to have robust, open-source infrastructure for science. XTX Markets is delighted to continue our support for arXiv in this important endeavor.
simon coyle, head of philanthropy, xtx markets
Siegel Family Endowment
Siegel Family Endowment has made a multi-year commitment to arXiv, advancing a shared vision for equitable digital infrastructure and open knowledge.
Open access to knowledge is a cornerstone of a healthy research ecosystem, but it is also essential to a thriving digital ecosystem and to ensuring people can equitably access and participate in the knowledge that shapes our world. We’re looking forward to supporting arXiv in its next chapter as essential infrastructure, enabling communities to share ideas, build on one another’s work, and sustain a living body of knowledge.
Joshua elder, svp & head of grantmaking at siegel family endowment
We are especially grateful to our
major funders
, who trust in arXiv’s important work, and are committed to our vision. Our major funders create a solid foundation of support and are an essential part of arXiv’s sustainable funding model, which is supplemented by our
membership program
, as well as
our sponsors
,
our affiliates
, and individual donors. Thank you for your unwavering support of arXiv!

data.title: Meta VR Glasses
data.author: polymorph1sm
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Meta 新款混合现实/AR眼镜的硬件规格、实际用途、佩戴体验，以及 Meta 的隐私与平台策略展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **硬件与生产力前景看好**：Micro-OLED、2412×2288分辨率、眼/手/面部追踪和外置计算盒，被认为可能比 Apple Vision Pro 更适合生产力工作；有人认为其价格也让 Steam Frame 等产品显得更合理。  
• **体验仍存疑**：70°×66°视场角可能产生“望远镜/面具”效果；舒适度、分辨率和长时间佩戴仍未达到替代实体屏幕的程度。外置计算盒体积较大，也影响便携性。  
• **实际价值受到质疑**：有人认为它没有解决明确问题，手势输入、虚拟多屏、看球赛等场景未必优于笔记本、手机、电视或便携显示器；在公共场合“对空操作”也可能尴尬。  
• **隐私与信任强烈反对**：多位评论者拒绝上传身份证，担心 Meta 收集大量个人信息；还担忧眼镜持续采集第一视角影像、录音并用于 AI 训练，甚至可能触及未经同意录音的法律问题。  
• **平台与开发者政策争议**：有人认可其采用 Oculus SDK、具备生态；但也批评 Meta 曾强制绑定 Facebook/要求验证身份、对开发者不友好，认为企业政策足以抵消硬件吸引力。  
• **内容与游戏是潜在亮点**：Beat Saber、Ace Attorney VR 等新内容引发期待，但评论者希望确认能否登陆 Quest 3 或 PCVR。

data.title: Linux support is coming to Snapdragon X2 Series
data.author: aaronday
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高通 Snapdragon X2 Elite 笔记本的性能潜力，以及 Linux/OpenBSD 支持是否能真正落地。

不同观点：
• 乐观派认为 X2 已接近甚至部分超过苹果 M 系列，明显强于英特尔和 AMD 同级产品；若能预装 Linux，将兼具高性能与长续航，适合小型笔记本、Surface 或 Framework 主板。  
• 支持进展派指出，OpenBSD 已实现部分 ACPI 下的 USB、键盘和触控板支持，Ubuntu 已确认 ARM EL2，可支持 KVM；高通也在上游推进 Hexagon NPU、Adreno GPU 等核心驱动。  
• 谨慎派担心重演第一代 X Elite：当初也承诺良好 Linux 支持，但最终未兑现，因此目前只能“谨慎乐观”。  
• 实用派要求标准发行版可直接替换原系统，驱动、固件和测试完整，不能依赖提取二进制或半专有方案；若 Wi-Fi、音频、摄像头 ISP 等统一由 SoC 管理，兼容性可能优于 Intel 平台。  
• 性能评价也有争议：有人称其接近 Apple M5 Pro，另一些人则批评 X 系列发布和生态建设远落后于苹果。

补充讨论：核心争议不在芯片性能，而在高通能否持续上游驱动、提供易安装且经过验证的 Linux 支持，并覆盖不同机型；游戏支持和 Framework 适配被视为潜在加分项。

data.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
data.author: raahelb
data.article_summary: Anthropic成立生命科学团队，利用Claude大规模分析DNA数据库并开展实验。约950个智能体在21小时内发现一种与噬菌体相关的新型酶系统“阵列关联逆转录酶”（ART）：逆转录酶基因旁存在重复DNA序列及辅助蛋白，特征类似CRISPR。其具体功能尚待研究，但可能具备可编程DNA操作潜力，展示了AI加速生物学发现的能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anthropic借助Claude发现与反转录酶相关的、带有CRISPR样重复序列的新型酶系统（ART），引发对科学价值、AI能力宣传及其产业影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• 科学价值较审慎：该成果主要是从已有基因组数据中发现新的基因组排列，寻找反转录酶本身并非极难；现有Cas9已较高效，真正限制治疗应用的是递送，因此距离医学转化仍很远。  
• AI能力受到肯定：AI能在大规模序列中筛选、比较不同反转录酶家族并发现异常模式，展示了“AI解析既有数据、辅助发现新生物学”的价值；有人认为公开代理运行记录中的即时反应，也可能成为未来科学史素材。  
• “Claude独立发现”受到质疑：评论强调这是“AI+人类”协作，研究人员负责问题设定、筛选、实验验证和命名。应明确说是Anthropic团队借助Claude发现，而非Claude单独完成。  
• 对宣传方式不满：营销白皮书、新闻稿及“Claude发现”“自主判断”等措辞被认为夸大能力、暗示意识或主体性；有人质疑为何不先投递Science、Nature等同行评审期刊。  
• 对Anthropic战略的担忧：公司可能从卖模型转向亲自做前沿科研，以成果改善AI形象、拓展商业模式，但也被批评有成为“什么都做”的公司之嫌。  
• 风险与社会影响：有人担心生物AI降低定向病毒制造门槛；另有评论担忧科研岗位、尤其待遇较低的博士后会受冲击。

补充讨论：争议核心是成果本身的科学分量、AI自主性的真实程度，以及公司是否在用夸张叙事包装“AI辅助科研”。

49820134.article_content:
Science
Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
Sep 23, 2026
We’re introducing a new life sciences research group and laboratory at Anthropic. Our focus is on fundamental biology research using Claude: exploring datasets of DNA to identify uncharacterized protein families, generating hypotheses at scale, and testing them through experiments in the lab. This post introduces the team behind this work and shares early results in which Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR, with only high-level direction from our scientists.
Many discoveries that have revolutionized biology and medicine started with a scientist noticing something odd in the staggering diversity of molecular machines found in nature. Restriction enzymes
,
proteins that cut DNA at specific short sequences
,
were found in bacterial immune systems, where they destroy the DNA of invading viruses. Researchers realized they could use these enzymes to cut DNA at chosen places and splice genes from one organism into another, which launched the biotechnology industry. Taq polymerase, an enzyme that copies DNA at high temperatures, was identified in a bacterium in a Yellowstone hotspring. It became the basis for PCR, the DNA-copying method used in much of modern diagnostics. CRISPR was first noticed as an unusual repeat sequence in the DNA of certain bacteria, and is now the foundation of gene editing-based medicines.
In the spring of 2026, we formed a research group to see whether general AI models can systematize and
accelerate such discoveries
. We believe that this acceleration will come from establishing a new way of doing biology research, in which agents collaborate with humans in every step of the process. Developing this new way of working required that we build our own lab and a single team working on everything from training Claude in biology to running experiments in the lab.
Today, we’re sharing early results from one of our first research programs, in which Claude autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system that is associated with an array of DNA repeats, a pattern reminiscent of CRISPR. Although we don’t yet know its function, the system that Claude discovered has a set of characteristics that have only ever been found together in a handful of other systems, all of which are programmable and perform operations like cutting, copying, and pasting DNA. Beyond CRISPR, which has already transformed science and medicine, several other such systems are now in development as promising tools.
The system that Claude found is based on a reverse transcriptase (RT), enzymes that copy RNA into DNA. While this underlying RT, found in a jumbo phage, had been identified in previous studies, Claude appears to be the first to notice the system’s defining features—an associated array of non-coding DNA sequences and an additional accessory protein of unknown function.
After reviewing the pre-print, Feng Zhang, one of the pioneers of CRISPR genome editing and a professor at MIT and the Broad Institute said:
This is an exciting example of how AI agents can contribute to biological discovery. The identification of RNA-repeat arrays associated with reverse transcriptases is genuinely intriguing and merits further investigation. I hope this work encourages more scientists to explore how AI can support their research.
We gave Claude a prompt to search through a massive database of DNA sequences for interesting new examples of RTs. Our involvement was limited to the initial prompt and the lab work, while Claude agents combed through the database, investigated the distinct RT families, and used their own judgement to identify interesting candidates. After 21 hours spent searching this data by roughly 950 agents using 210 million tokens, one of the agents spotted something remarkable: a repeating pattern of DNA sequences that occurs next to the gene for an odd-looking RT. After further analysis and testing in our lab, we recognized that this pattern marked a previously uncharacterized enzyme system found in bacteriophages (the viruses that infect bacteria) that we call array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART).
Our work to understand the primary function of ARTs is ongoing. However, we think it is important to share such findings early, both to demonstrate Claude’s capabilities and to give the broader community insight into what we’re working on. We have released a pre-print (
here
) that discusses this in more detail.
About our lab
We are a team of scientists who have spent our careers exploring unusual proteins, and specialize in using computational approaches to systematically read DNA, interpret its evolution, and pick out biological systems for further characterization. Our research prior to joining Anthropic has helped to better understand the
evolution
and
regulation
of CRISPR systems, discover new
enzymes
for next-generation
cell and gene therapies

data.title: VSCode's SSH Agent Is Bananas (2025)
data.author: Rapzid
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 VSCode 通过 SSH 远程开发的机制：它会在远端下载并运行包含 Node 的代理，通过 SSH 端口转发与本地通信，代理可访问文件、编辑内容、启动终端并持久化。作者认为，这种权限远超简单远程编辑，存在较大安全风险，尤其不适合生产环境。文章也指出，隔离的云端环境更适合运行能自我迭代的 LLM 编程代理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VS Code Remote-SSH/SSH Agent 的架构是否会破坏“远程沙箱”安全边界，以及这种设计究竟是合理功能还是高风险后门。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为，远程开发本就需要在远端运行扩展、命令、容器、安装包、端口转发等；通过 SSH 隧道传输并部署 VS Code Server 是无法假设远端可联网时的自然方案。只要远端可信、权限限制得当，这些“缺点”正是功能优势，适合团队开发和生产环境以外的场景。  
• 安全担忧者指出，真正危险的不是本地前端控制远端，而是被攻陷的远端可反向利用 WebSocket/Remote-SSH 在本地执行代码、读写文件或持久化。微软也明确警告只能连接可信远端，因此 VM 或“沙箱”并不能自动保护本机。  
• 有人认为该架构本身可以接受，但反向执行绝不可接受；也有人主张让 LLM 只能在工作目录内操作，或只通过可审计的 CLI“输入”，而非授予完整 VS Code 能力。  
• 另有评论质疑为何不用 SSHFS，并提出 VSCodium 扩展是否存在同类风险；也有人认为文章误解了 VS Code/SSH 的设计，甚至将其夸张比作 rootkit。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“远程主机是否可信”与“沙箱边界是否真实存在”，以及评论者对 SSH Agent 和 LLM Agent 的概念混淆。

49822555.article_content:
Author
Name
Thomas Ptacek
@tqbf
@tqbf
Weâre interested in getting integrated into the flow VSCode uses to do remote editing over SSH, because everybody is using VSCode now, and, in particular, theyâre using forks of VSCode that generate code with LLMs.
âhallucinationâ is what we call it when LLMs get code wrong; âengineeringâ is what we call it when people do.
LLM-generated code is
useful in the general case
if you know what youâre doing. But itâs ultra-useful if you can close the loop between the LLM and the execution environment (with an âAgentâ setup). Thereâs lots to say about this, but for the moment: itâs a semi-effective antidote to hallucination: the LLM generates the code, the agent scaffolding runs the code, the code generates errors, the agent feeds it back to the LLM, the process iterates.
So, obviously, the issue here is you donât want this iterative development process happening on your development laptop, because LLMs have boundary issues, and theyâll iterate on your system configuration just as happily on the Git project you happen to be working in. A thing youâd really like to be able to do: run a closed-loop agent-y (âagenticâ? is that what we say now) configuration for an LLM, on a clean-slate Linux instance that spins up instantly and that canât screw you over in any way. You get where weâre going with this.
Anyways! I would like to register a concern.
Emacs hosts the spiritual forebearer of remote editing systems, a blob of hyper-useful Elisp called
âTrampâ
. If you can hook Tramp up to any kind of interactive environment â usually, an SSH session â where it can run Bourne shell commands, it can extend Emacs to that environment.
So, VSCode has a feature like Tramp. Which, neat, right? Youâd think, take Tramp, maybe simplify it a bit, switch out Elisp for Typescript.
Youâd think wrong!
Unlike Tramp, which lives off the land on the remote connection, VSCode mounts a full-scale invasion: it runs a Bash snippet stager that downloads an agent, including a binary installation of Node.
I
think
this is
the source code
?
The agent runs over port-forwarded SSH. It establishes a WebSockets connection back to your running VSCode front-end. The underlying protocol on that connection can:
Wander around the filesystem
Edit arbitrary files
Launch its own shell PTY processes
Persist itself
In security-world, thereâs a name for tools that work this way. I wonât say it out loud, because thatâs not fair to VSCode, but letâs just say the name is murid in nature.
I would be a little nervous about letting people VSCode-remote-edit stuff on dev servers, and apoplectic if that happened during an incident on something in production.
It turns out we donât have to care about any of this to get a custom connection to a Fly Machine working in VSCode, so none of this matters in any kind of deep way, but: weâve decided to just be a blog again, so: we had to learn this, and now you do too.

Did Semgrep Just Get A Lot More Interesting?

AI GPU Clusters, From Your Laptop, With Livebook

data.title: The "Windows XP Box" (2003)
data.author: doubletwoyou
data.article_summary: 文章介绍作者将一台Mini-ITX电脑装进Windows XP软件包装盒的过程。整机尺寸仅243×200×48毫米，采用EPIA M10000主板，并要求内置光驱、不能裁剪主板、外壳不变形且散热安全。由于空间极其狭小，作者通过精密规划各部件位置，使用易加工的3毫米Wonderboard塑料制作内部支撑框架，完成硬盘、电源、主板和光驱的紧凑组装。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕2003年前后的定制 Mini-ITX 电脑展开，讨论其创意、紧凑设计、怀旧价值，以及当代硬件和定制文化的变化。

不同观点：
• 怀旧赞赏：多数评论认为这类机器兼具“荒诞感”和创造力，Mini-ITX 当年能在极小空间集成丰富功能，令人印象深刻；有人还回忆 Shuttle XPC、啤酒箱电脑等类似作品。  
• 创意稀缺的批评：有人认为如今3D打印电脑外壳大多只是普通机箱、机架或开放式平台，缺少过去定制作品的想象力；现代电脑外观也趋于千篇一律。  
• 技术亮点：硬件开关实现 Windows XP 与 Red Hat Linux 双启动，被认为是整机最精彩的设计之一；评论者曾因这项改装在少年时期感到“神奇”。  
• 时代与形式变化：有人指出如今 Micro-ATX 可能比 Mini-ITX 更普及，也有人期待现代技术重新带来类似作品。  
• 复古网页与实体软件：旧式网站设计、软件盒装销售都引发怀旧，有人甚至觉得复古视觉风格与优质内容存在关联。

补充讨论：评论者提醒文章最后一页最值得阅读；整体讨论并无明显争议，主要分歧在于对当代定制硬件创意是否衰退的评价。

The "Windows XP Box"
By Andy France
Posted on December 1, 2003
Jump to:
Introduction
The Back Panel
The Motherboard
Finishing Touches
Introduction
I needed a small Windows XP machine and a Mini-ITX board was the obvious choice. So I decided to build my "Windows XP Box" in a Windows XP box. The external dimensions of the box are a tiny 243mm x 200mm x 48mm.
My requirements were:
Use as powerful a motherboard as possible for the size i.e. a Nehemiah EPIA M10000.
It must have an internal CD drive (this size eating requirement turned out be be very hard to meet).
No bits could be cut off the motherboard to make it fit.
The box must not bulge in an unsightly way, nor can the box be made bigger.
It must not burst into flames when working hard (this should always be a requirement of a computer project).
Fortunately there is no longer any requirement for an internal floppy drive. That would have have defeated me.
Construction
The bits arrive and it looks like an impossible task, with too many bits to fit in a small space.
I nearly gave up and decided it was an impossible task. The Windows XP box was 3mm thinner and 12 mm narrower than the Adobe Acrobat box I had measured up when first deciding if the project was going to be possible. The challenge was to arrange the components into a 3D jigsaw, then decide how to build enough of an internal support case to get everything to stay in place.
Eventually it looked like I might have a possible layout, but the tolerances were tight. I had 6mm to spare on the long internal dimension of the box and only 3mm to spare on the thickness of the box, and this was not allowing for any thickness for the internal support case that holds everything in place.
In order to mount all the bits I was going to have to make an inner support case that would tightly slide into the cardboard box. I chose Wonderboard plastic as my construction material because it is reasonably strong and very easy to work with (it cuts with a Stanley knife). It would have been nice to use aluminium, but the cramped design made the chances of a short circuit too great.
The first construction step was to cut out a base plate the exact size of the inside of the cardboard box and double check where the bits will fit.
As the Wonderboard was 3mm thick this reduced my tolerance in two dimensions to zero. The CD drive would touch one side of the inner support case. The deep part of the CD drive would touch the heat sink on the motherboard, with the narrow bit being able to overlap it, and the far side of the motherboard touches the other side of the Wonderboard case. In the other dimension it was even harder. The top of the sound connector would touch the support case, and the underside of the motherboard would touch the cardboard box. data.title: We just shipped support for the ugliest part of HTTP: Vary
data.author: thisisfatih
data.article_summary: 文章介绍 HTTP 响应头 Vary：它能让缓存根据请求头区分语言、格式等不同响应，避免返回错误内容，但按原始值区分会造成缓存变体爆炸、命中率下降。Cloudflare 将 Vary 支持加入 Cache Rules，允许用户规范化协商请求头、精确透传必要差异，或对不可预测的变化绕过缓存，从而在正确性与缓存效率间取得平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare开始支持基于HTTP `Vary`响应头的缓存分流，解决同一URL按请求头返回不同格式时的缓存混淆问题。

不同观点：
• **长期期待、持肯定态度**：simonw、xyzzy_plugh认为这是迟来的重要功能。过去Cloudflare基本忽略非图片资源的`Vary`，可能把JSON缓存后错误提供给需要HTML的用户；该功能被视为真正内容协商的实现。  
• **偏好显式URL区分格式**：simonw虽认可功能，但实际选择不用“根据`Accept`返回HTML/JSON”的模式，而是通过`.json`后缀明确区分URL，使缓存和行为更可预测。  
• **关注实现细节和潜在风险**：rob-olmos指出，若部分源站响应没有`Vary`，Cloudflare会正常缓存，可能与带`Vary`的缓存对象发生冲突，甚至“抢先命中”。他询问是否应通过规则确保所有响应都带`Vary`。  
• **分享实践与反思**：bhouston表示曾在CloudFront上成功使用`Vary`，却误以为Cloudflare也支持，结果给其SaaS应用造成严重bug；jrochkind1则感叹`Vary`机制复杂，认为现代Web能正常运行已很不容易。  
• **附带批评**：rgbrenner认可功能上线，但讽刺Cloudflare应顺便修好营销邮件退订功能。

补充讨论：争议焦点集中在“缺少`Vary`的响应如何与分区缓存共存”以及是否应统一补充响应头；评论总体支持该功能，但也强调显式URL方案更稳妥。

49823195.article_content:
The response header,
Vary
, has been called â
the ugliest part of HTTP that we haven't yet improved.
â The same post describes it as a âhorrible, kludgy mechanismâ with âpretty abysmal interoperabilityâ across intermediaries. That is usually where sensible engineers back away slowly with their hands raised.Â
Thatâs not exactly an endorsement of
Vary
, but ugly doesnât mean useless.Â
One URL can have more than one correct response. A server might, for example, deliver different image formats to different browsers. If a cache ignores
Vary
, it risks serving the wrong bytes to a request. But if it treats every raw header value as distinct, a handful of similar requests can spread into thousands of barely reusable cache entries.
Vary
tells a cache which request fields may affect the response, but it does not tell the cache which differences
actually matter.
Vary
support is now available in
Cache Rules
on every plan. The origin still names the request headers that may affect a response, but you decide how Cloudflare handles each one. You can normalize known negotiation headers, pass exact values through when those small differences matter, or bypass cache when the variation is too unpredictable. The origin declares what may vary, and you decide how much variation is actually meaningful for the cache.
How Vary works
Vary
is a
standard
HTTP response header that tells intermediary caches (like Cloudflare) which request fields may affect the response sent by the origin. Sites use
Vary
to serve different languages, image formats, compression schemes, or regional content from the same URL.
Take one URL that produces two valid representations. A browser requests a webpage:
GET /catalog HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Accept: text/html
The origin returns HTML and identifies
Accept
as a field that may affect the response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600
Vary: Accept
An API client can request the same URL with a different preference:
GET /catalog HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Accept: application/json
This time, the correct response is JSON. The
Vary: Accept
header tells the cache that the URL alone is not enough to choose between responses. The requestâs
Accept
value must also be considered.
Without
Vary
, whichever response enters the cache first can be served to both clients. If HTML wins, the API client receives markup and its JSON parser fails. If JSON wins, a browser expecting a web page receives an API response.
Vary
prevents the cache from serving the wrong response to the requesting client. But it introduces a harder question: when two requests contain different header values, do they actually
need
different responses?
When correct caching becomes useless
Vary can tell a cache which request fields may affect a response. It does not tell the cache what the response represents. For example, take an origin that serves content in only English, French, and German. A client might send:
Accept-Language: en-US, fr;q=0.8
While another client might request:
Accept-Language: fr;q=0.8, en-GB
Both requests prefer English here. The originâs response may map both requests to exactly the same English response. But a cache comparing the raw values cannot safely assume they are equivalent. They have different orders and
language tags
(that the origin doesnât differentiate). So the cache may store them as separate variants, even when their response bodies contain identical bytes.
This is
Vary
âs central problem. Applications often produce a small, finite set of representations from an enormous set of possible request values. The origin understands that thousands of language preferences collapse into three supported languages, while a cache usually does not.
This problem compounds when a response varies on multiple fields. Ten possible values across one field create ten variants. Ten values across three fields can create 1,000 combinations. Real headers can have far greater cardinality:
User-Agent
values are numerous, cookies can be unique to individual visitors, and preference headers can differ in ordering, formatting (spaces and tabs matter!), and
quality values
.
The result is a cache that can be perfectly correct and almost permanently cold (an entry never reused). Identical responses can be scattered across entries that receive too little traffic to remain hot and in cache. They can consume capacity,
evict
one another, reduce cache hit ratios, and send more requests back to origin servers. Eviction can remove cold entries, but it cannot merge them just because the responses are identical.Â
An analysis
of more than 120 million responses from nearly 50,000 popular sites found almost 3,000 sites varying on four or more fields. Some varied on 10, 23, or even 47 fields. We want to make sure that customers have the tools they need to use
Vary
when appropriate, but not so much that they create a useless cache.Â

data.title: Fixing the Portobello Police Station Clock
data.author: avidly
data.article_summary: 作者受邀前往波多贝罗旧警察局，协助社区修复钟楼。经攀爬探索，他们发现钟表可能始建于1877年，后改用电机和控制盒驱动。通过解除齿轮棘爪成功校准时间，并研究出报时系统由电机、开关和微控制器控制。文章也介绍了建筑的历史及其转为社区所有后的修缮工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇介绍老建筑/警察局机械装置的文章，讨论设备维护、安全监控、技术状况，以及文章带来的社区兴趣和怀旧感。

不同观点：
• 维护安全派：建议在木梯或踏板上加自粘防滑砂纸，成本低却能显著降低跌倒风险；并建议用PoE摄像头持续观察齿轮和状态灯，配合Frigate等软件实现低侵入监控。
• 电池更换派：多位评论者认为照片中的12V、7–8Ah AGM电池与报警器或消防楼梯照明电池相同，长期满充且可能受高温影响，若无更换记录就应尽快更换；但若只是备用电源、供电稳定，老化未必立即影响运行。
• 电路技术派：有人推测电路板是小公司或手工制作的老产品，单面板、无丝印、元件和导线直接焊接，虽不够规范，但若设备静止、无明显市电安全问题，仍可能继续使用。状态灯“长长短短短”被猜测为摩斯码“7”，但缺乏时间变化等证据。
• 文化兴趣派：许多人赞赏文章的写法和“早期互联网黑客精神”，也因设备位于家乡而感到亲切，并询问如何参与本地社区项目。
• 延伸分享派：评论者推荐Fred Dibnah探索大本钟、巴尔的摩Bromo Seltzer塔的重力钟，以及钟楼设备维修故事。

补充讨论：有人分享教堂阁楼灰尘导致机场安检报警的经历，也有“蘑菇为何有警察局”等幽默调侃。

49817469.article_content:
Written on 11th April 2026
I got a message from a friend today which read along the lines of "I know we were going to meet in Edinburgh today, but do you fancy meeting in Portobello instead and trying to fix the clock in the old police station with me?"
I don't know about you, but clambering around the dusty nineteenth century clock tower of an abandoned police station sounds an ideal way to spend a Saturday afternoon to me, so I jumped at the chance.
The rather grand
Portobello Police Station
building.
This was in response to a message from
Action Porty
:
"Can you help keep Portobello on time? Action Porty has recently bought the Police Station for the community, but we can't work out how to change the time on the clock tower! We wondered if there was anyone in the community with expertise that could advise us of the details for changing the time? Or who best to contact for help?"
The bit I hadn't figured out was that clocks are high up. If we were to fix the clock we would be next to it and so we would also be high up. And being high up involves heights, and steep long ladders are needed to get up high.
I suppressed my whimpers at climbing up the rather high, steep ladder into the likely spider-infested darkness and was rewarded with an explore of the attic, which lead to another set of steps which went to the clock tower itself.
Once there we were rewarded with the magnificent sight of the clock mechanism and its three clock faces:
Construction of the building apparently started in 1877 and it seems quite feasible that this was an original mechanism. Modifications had been made - electric motors powered the mechanism and a control box allowed the clock chime to be turned off overnight.
The building was built to house meeting, administration and courts for Portobello burgh council. After Portobello was absorbed into Edinburgh the building became a library, and then a police station.
The Scottish Land Fund has since enabled it to be purchased for community ownership and when I went there many volunteeers were removing the 1970s polystyrene ceiling tiles and wood-chip wallpaper to reveal the original grandeur of the building.
Setting the clock
The first step was to figure out how to set the time. This is probably easy to someone in the know, but we weren't.
We figured that the clock is driven from the small motor, through a series of gears onto a shaft which rotates once per hour. This shaft is split into three - one for each face, and drives the minute hand directly. A gear on each clock face derives the hour hand. If we could disconnect the motor maybe we could turn the shaft directly and set the time.
Sure enough - we found a pawl on one of the gears which could be lifted out of the way. Once this was done the shaft turned easily and we could set the time. Each hand had a counterweight on the clock face and we could set the time by imagining the hand we couldn't see opposite to each counterweight.
We had a slightly stupid moment when we thought we'd got it wrong, and the clock was running backwards - only to realise we were inside the clock and so were looking at it the wrong way. Doh. We had to head down to the ground to check that the time was correct - but - phew - time was OK and not running backwards.
Setting the chime
Figuring out the chime was more difficult. The original mechanism had been modified, and switches and a motor had been added. These led to a box containing a circuit board which definitely was not from 1877. It contained a PIC 16F628 microcontroller which had a suspected date-code of 2001. There were a number of relays, a power supply and a battery charging circuit to charge the included lead-acid battery. I assume this box would be getting on for 1/4 century old, but it still seemed to work. No idea how good the battery was; maybe this should be tested another time.
We have idea who designed and built this box; there were no obvious description markings. Is it a standard thing, or just a one-off for this clock?
A mystery unmarked circuit board, ripe for deciphering.

data.title: LensVLM: Compressing long context as images, expanding only relevant pages
data.author: victormustar
data.article_summary: LensVLM-9B是一款9B参数视觉语言模型，针对压缩文本图像进行理解。它先扫描压缩页面，再通过学习到的工具识别并选择性还原相关页面，以降低视觉信息处理成本、扩展有效上下文。模型基于Qwen架构微调，支持5倍、10倍和15倍压缩，适用于文档问答等任务。项目提供代码、推理示例及评测资料，模型采用BF16格式，遵循苹果机器学习研究模型许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕视觉编码与KV缓存压缩、分块及细节缩放机制的实现思路展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [taylorfinley]指出，这种方法并非全新，Oh My Pi 已经实践了一段时间，并称之为“Snap compact”，强调其已有先例。  
• [rao-v]总体赞同该方法，将视觉编码器类比为成本较高、但保真度更高的RAG编码器。其进一步设想：训练模型使其对页面级KV缓存的排列顺序不敏感，即无论各页面KV缓存以何种顺序输入，模型都能理解每一页内容。这样可把视觉编码页面的KV缓存直接作为模型推理的“块”，并自然扩展“放大查看、获取更多细节”等机制。  
• [lathoa]认为该方法有趣，对其思路表示感谢和认可，但未提出具体技术观点。

补充讨论：评论整体基调积极，主要差异在于：一方强调已有类似实践，另一方则着重提出未来的技术改进方向。潜在讨论焦点是KV缓存的页面级组织方式，以及如何实现排列不变性并支持渐进式细节获取。

data.title: Mercury 2.5 LLM hits 770 tokens per second
data.author: Retro_Dev
data.article_summary: 文章评测了 Inception 的专有模型 Mercury 2.5。其智能指数为12分，在175个同类模型中排名91，略低于平均水平；输出速度达770 tokens/秒，排名第2，表现突出。输入价格为每百万tokens 0.25美元，输出0.75美元，成本适中，并支持26万tokens上下文。模型仅支持文本输入输出，具备推理能力，但整体智能性一般，优势在于速度快、价格合理、输出简洁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕该扩散式大语言模型的速度、性能、成本与实际价值展开争论。

不同观点：
• 速度优势派：认为模型推理速度极快，Cerebras 上的 gpt-oss-120b 可达约1400 token/s；有人实际体验后称其“快得惊人”，适合趣味或对延迟敏感的项目。  
• 性价比质疑派：指出其输入/输出价格为0.25/0.75美元，明显高于 DeepSeek V4 Flash、Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next 等同类开放权重模型，且后者在170GB内存内即可部署，因此看不出采用它的理由。  
• 性能怀疑派：认为它可能只是取得与 gpt-oss-120b 相近的基准成绩，却未必更快；即便速度很高，若综合能力在前沿模型中接近垫底，速度也没有实际意义。  
• 技术路线反对派：认为扩散式LLM可能是“走不通的方向”，Google曾尝试但未持续投入，尚未看到其明显优于传统自回归模型的应用场景。  
• 少数正面评价：有人认为模型本身表现“还不错”，并强调极高吞吐量确实具有观赏性和潜在价值。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“极致速度能否弥补模型能力、价格和部署效率上的劣势”，以及扩散式LLM究竟是否存在明确的帕累托优势。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利重启核能、建立小型模块化反应堆（SMR）监管框架的可行性、经济性与政治动机。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为核能可提供稳定电力，SMR更安全、灵活、建设较快；核能不应与太阳能“非此即彼”，适合土地有限、工业用电需求高或需能源安全的国家，并可促进欧盟、北约合作。  
• 怀疑者指出，目前几乎没有已商业运行的SMR，成本和工期缺乏验证；法国NUWARD预估约115美元/MWh，可能依赖补贴，难与不断降价的风光储能竞争。  
• 多名评论者担心项目成为利益输送：借研发、设计和取消合同制造赔偿，最终由政府和纳税人承担，而非真正发电盈利。  
• 反核立场强调长期安全、核废料处置及意大利地震风险，且该国尚无国家级核废料最终储存设施。  
• 另有观点认为核电站在战争中相对不易被摧毁，具有战略资产价值，即使经济上亏损也可能被保留。

补充讨论：争议焦点是核能究竟是必要的能源安全工具，还是高成本、未成熟且容易被政治和资本操弄的项目；意大利民众对核能的态度也被认为受切尔诺贝利事故和“文化战争”影响。

• [bartread]认为，框架自制滚动条常因疏忽而功能缩水、行为不一致；Windows自2007年前后进入UI框架混乱期，亟需恢复跨应用的一致体验。其选择Rust+Qt，主要看重性能和相对稳定性。  
• [mrob]主张点击滚动槽默认应“滚动到点击位置”，因为PageUp/PageDown已有键盘快捷键，鼠标应提供独有功能；认为GTK做得对，而Qt不对。  
• 多位评论者补充了平台差异：Windows原生控件支持Shift+点击等隐藏操作；GTK中点击槽可定位、Shift+点击相当于翻页；Qt、Firefox、LibreOffice、Inkscape、Office等实现各不相同。有人指出Office甚至不支持“滚动到此处”，Excel滚动条问题尤甚。  
• [butz]批评网页使用过细或隐藏滚动条，认为损害可发现性；[lastscattering]则以自身网站为例，说明自定义滚动体验很容易不完整或做坏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点是“滚动到此处”应否作为默认行为，以及不同系统/应用应否统一。  
• Shift+点击、右键菜单、中键、拖动取消等功能鲜为人知，且版本和应用间不一致。评论建议建立标准控件隐藏行为文档，供重实现者参考。

data.title: Making Tailscale Faster
data.author: yarapavan
data.article_summary: Tailscale介绍新一轮性能优化：通过避免小数据包复制、缩短队列，Linux和Android网络性能提升约5%，并降低内存占用。基于此，将为子网路由器、应用连接器和出口节点引入多队列并行处理，提升吞吐量、降低延迟、充分利用多核资源。文章还预告了后续客户端及性能工具改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Tailscale/WireGuard 的性能、实现路线、资源消耗及实际使用体验展开争论。

不同观点：
• **性能批评**：iscoelho 认为 Tailscale 最大问题是速度不足：Windows/Mac 客户端难超 1Gbps，Linux 在大包合成测试中也难达 10Gbps，混合流量（IMIX）下更不具竞争力；他认为内核 WireGuard、IPsec、DPDK/XDP 和零拷贝网络都能显著提升性能。  
• **反驳“内核必然更快”**：Tailscale 联合创始人 apenwarr 指出，用户态 wireguard-go 曾因优化优于内核 WireGuard，双方也已互相吸收改进。极高带宽场景长期更适合 DPDK 等用户态方案，内核模式并非绝对优势。  
• **协议层瓶颈观点**：apenwarr 进一步指出，WireGuard 使用的加密套件缺乏硬件加速支持，若要达到数百 Gbps，可能需要改变数据包格式；未来支持后量子密码时或可一并解决。  
• **简洁性与实际体验**：fitblipper 认为直接部署原生 WireGuard 更稳定、更快、配置简单，尤其避免手机端 DNS 问题，因此 Tailscale 的便利性对其已失去吸引力。  
• **其他需求与疑虑**：aborsy 希望降低出口节点的电池消耗；CharlesW 询问其 Linux/Android 优化是否限制了跨平台表现；ykurtov 报告约 250 个会话、仅 60MB/s 流量时延迟就急剧上升。

补充讨论：争议核心是“内核实现是否必然更快”，以及 Tailscale 是否愿意投入高性能网络优化；评论既涉及理论峰值，也反映稳定性、移动端功耗和多会话扩展性等实际问题。

49819880.article_content:
Blog
|
product
September 22, 2026
We’re making Tailscale faster
Authors
Kabir Sikand
Kevin Purdy
Contributors
Alex Valiushko
Claus Lensbøl
Michael J. Fromberger
Jordan Whited
If you’ve been following Tailscale at all, you know we’re really just a bunch of geeks who care a lot about internet connectivity. One thing we love to talk about is NAT Traversal. That’s one of the core value-adds with Tailscale:
we tamed NAT
. Not every network is friendly, but Tailscale can still find a path in a wide range of conditions. That’s not the only important thing for an internet protocol: the data plane also has to be performant.
Over the years we’ve been investing in making Tailscale fast. We started by
increasing TCP throughput on Linux devices
. Then we made significant breakthroughs in wireguard-go to
surpass 10Gb/s
on bare metal. We later leveraged segmentation offloads to
increase throughput over 4x
for UDP-based applications. Alongside these improvements to our data plane, we built primitives like
Tailscale Peer Relays
, which can
improve network performance in tricky conditions
.
All of this has made Tailscale practical for more performance-sensitive workloads. It means you can use Tailscale for continuous integration, agentic workflows, remote development environments, robotic edge devices, heavy data and telemetry workloads, and more. Tailscale helps those devices connect across a wide range of network conditions.
So yeah, we think Tailscale is fast. But we also think we can make it faster.
Today we’ll detail how we’re boosting throughput for app connectors, subnet routers, and exit nodes, with some multi-queue technology (landing in the second half of 2026). We’ll also preview some throughput and memory overhead improvements we’re deploying in upcoming stable client releases. And we’ll look at some performance tooling issues we want to solve for our customers.
Less memory overhead for small packets
Most network packets are tiny, like 1 KiB. But to use Linux’s most efficient throughput tools, like Generic Receive Offload (GRO), Tailscale has to be ready to accept 64 KiB of traffic at once. It’s a bit like container shipping: the ports, ships, and trucks are built for one container shape, however full it happens to be.
Tailscale has to unpack those containers—every packet gets decrypted and delivered on its own. The wireguard-go implementation that informs Tailscale’s cryptography and networking essentials, only offers one 64 KiB buffer size to unpack into. So a 1 KiB packet is copied into its own 64 KiB buffer, every time. That’s a rich optimization target.
On Linux and Android, Tailscale now leaves those packets where they landed. It identifies where each one starts and ends inside the single large read instead of copying it somewhere new. Small packets stay small in memory, many share one allocation, and they spend less time being copied. In itself, this led to a roughly 5% speed-up in many network configurations.
Separately, we shortened packet queues—the lines packets wait in between stages of the pipeline. The queues are there to absorb bursts of traffic. Testing showed that most of that depth went unused, while shorter queues meant less waiting time and less memory overhead.
What do we do with all that freed-up memory space? We passed the savings on to some of the hardest-working nodes: subnet routers and app connectors.
Multi-queue for subnet routers, app connectors, and exit nodes
Subnet routers
can look completely different across different tailnets. For someone running a small homelab network, a subnet router can easily handle a small set of
192.168.x.y
non-Tailscale devices. A subnet router that fronts a cloud deployment, one with hundreds of peers, will carry substantially more traffic.
Until recently, subnet routers, app connectors, and exit nodes processed packets for multiple independent streams in one ordered, single-thread pipeline. That meant a single lane was shared across many connections, because a receiving application must never see its own packets arrive out of order.
Having reduced our memory footprint, we had capacity to implement a multi-queue system: several lanes instead of one, scaled to the machine’s resources rather than the number of peers. Each stream of packets gets a lane and stays there, while the lanes run in parallel, allowing work to spread across CPU cores.
It results in higher aggregate capacity and lower delay between receiving and forwarding packets for subnet routers and app connectors. Hardware you already have gets used more efficiently. App connectors and exit nodes, typically serving many users with short-lived connections, get a particularly noticeable boost.
“This translates into lower latency, essentially faster processing of data from the moment we read it off the wire to the moment we send it to the OS,” said Alex Valiushko, member of technical staff at Tailscale.

data.title: Radicle: Disclosure of Vulnerability in the Network Protocol
data.author: lostmsu
data.article_summary: Radicle披露两项影响所有已发布版本的严重漏洞：节点间通信未加密，可能泄露传输中的仓库内容；握手认证失效，攻击者可冒充获准节点获取私有仓库。建议立即停止使用和播种私有仓库，视已传输内容为泄露并轮换凭据；Tor、VPN等无法彻底防护。修复版将是不兼容的重大版本，正在开发中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Radicle 节点间网络流量未加密、未认证，导致私有仓库内容可能被路径观察者读取，暴露出安全设计、披露流程和项目成熟度问题。

不同观点：
• **严重安全缺陷批评**：多位评论者认为，在强调密码学身份和去中心化的项目中，竟遗漏最基本的传输加密，近乎“忘了加密”，不像普通协议漏洞，更像设计失误。  
• **披露与应对不当**：漏洞于6月24日报告，却约三个月后才公告；临时建议是停止通过网络使用私有仓库，甚至假设其内容已泄露，被批评为反应迟缓、影响严重。  
• **对项目质量和安全实践失去信任**：有人连同自定义协议、`curl | shell` 安装方式、加密货币/DAO背景一起质疑其专业性，表示不会再用于私密数据。  
• **倾向采用成熟方案**：评论欢迎改用 iroh，也有人建议使用基于 QUIC 的 mTLS，认为标准化协议和成熟证书验证生态能避免“自研协议”陷阱，并可能改善流量隐蔽性。  
• **潜在连带影响**：有人担忧复用 `netservices.rs` 的 Nym、Farcaster 等项目是否也错误地以为流量已认证加密。

49817524.article_content:
Radicle is a peer-to-peer, local-first code
collaboration stack built on Git.
Summary
What happened?
Two critical security vulnerabilities in the network protocol used by Radicle nodes were reported.
Which versions are affected?
All versions of Radicle
that were released to date are vulnerable.
What is the issue?
Network traffic between nodes is
not
encrypted and
not
authenticated.
Authentication of repository contents via Signed References still detects if attackers along the network path between two nodes modify objects in transit.
Thus, the main concern is information leakage, i.e., attackers along the network path between two nodes
reading
objects in transit.
For public repositories, information leakage is less of a concern.
However, encryption in transit is crucial for private repositories.
What should users do?
We recommend to stop using private repositories until a fix is released.
When will the fixed version be released?
Due to a lack of version negotiation features, combined with the fix being incompatible on the wire, a backward compatible mitigation is not feasible; that means the release to fix this issue will be breaking, thus bump the major version number.
Work towards this is under way.
With this disclosure, our goal is, first and foremost, to be honest and clear about the situation, so that users can assess and act accordingly, while we are working on a
resolution
.
The vulnerabilities
The network protocol used by Radicle does not give the confidentiality it was expected to give. Anyone who can observe the network path between two nodes can read the data they exchange as the data is sent in plain text. This was reported to us by Konstantinos Maninakis on 2026-06-24. You can read his post about the issue at
https://maninak.com/blog/radicle-cleartext-transport-vulnerability/
. We reported upstream, see
this issue
.
Peer authentication in the connection handshake is broken and allows impersonation. An attacker can connect to your node and present a Node ID that is not its own. Private repositories are shared only with allow-listed Node IDs. An attacker who fakes an allow-listed Node ID can fetch a private repository directly, without being on the network path. This was reported to us by cryptocode on 2026-08-12. We proposed a fix upstream, see
this pull request
.
The second flaw is harder to exploit on its own than it sounds. To impersonate an allow-listed Node ID, an attacker must first know one. The allow-list is not public, so an attacker who is not on the network path has to guess.
In practice, the two flaws are most useful when they can be exploited together: an attacker on the path sees the Node IDs at both ends of a connection, and both are normally on the allow-list.
That attacker can read whatever is exchanged while they watch, and can then use a Node ID they saw to fetch the whole repository on demand.
The realistic threat is anyone on the path between your node and node it syncs with, and no setting or allow-list protects against them.
We are publishing this before the security update is available. You can act on it today, and no fix we release later can undo an exposure that has already happened.
Workaround
Stop using private repositories (over the network) until the security update is released.
Stop seeding private repositories, as described below.
However, you may want to keep your private repositories in storage, i.e., not delete them entirely, so that you may start seeding them again once a fixed version is released.
Consider every private repository you have transmitted over the network to another node leaked.
If it contained unencrypted credentials, keys, or tokens, rotate them.
Using additionally encrypted transports, such as Tor, I2P, or other overlay networks or VPN solutions are not sufficient to protect your data.
They hide network traffic from an attacker along the network path between two nodes.
Even though that limits the attack surface, this does not prevent peer impersonation, and a targeted, sophisticated attack might lead to exfiltratation of the contents of private repositories.
How to stop seeding private repositories
List the private repositories in storage:
rad
ls
--private
--all
Change the seeding policy of very individual repository to âblockâ:
rad block <RID>
Note:
We recommend to use
rad block
instead of
rad unseed
, in case the seeding policy of your node is set to
allow
.
rad unseed
removes the seeding policy for a repository, and your node then falls back to its default policy.
The default is
block
, so on a default configuration
rad unseed
is enough.
If you changed the default seeding policy to
allow
, your node keeps serving the repository after you unseed it.
rad block
sets an explicit block, which the node checks first, so it works either way.
To stop the node completely:
rad node stop
Three limits on what this achieves:
It stops your node from serving the repository.
It does not delete your local copy. The copy stays in
$(rad path)/storage/<RID

data.title: The mystery animal on an ancient god's head
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章探讨埃及神祇塞特头上的神秘动物形象。其特征包括竖耳、硬尾和下弯长鼻，可能源自猎犬、驴、猪、骆驼甚至已灭绝动物，也可能完全是艺术虚构。塞特象征混乱，既与奥西里斯和荷鲁斯为敌，又保护太阳神拉。由于时代变迁、外族征服及相关形象被毁，这一谜团至今无定论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕埃及神祇塞特（Setesh）的动物形象展开讨论，包括其真实原型、象征意义、历史来源及文章呈现质量。

不同观点：
• 传统考据观点：认为塞特的形象明显更像狗或豺；塞特与利比亚及“混乱、敌对的神祇”相关，因此其原型可能来自利比亚地区。撒哈拉沙漠不断扩张，相关遗迹或许仍被掩埋，现阶段难以下定论。  
• 多重原型观点：有人认为塞特的动物形象可能本就具有混合特征，吻部像鸟类或爬行动物，耳朵则难以辨认，因此不能简单归为狗或豺。  
• 象征主义观点：塞特的形态源自“混沌”，会随观看者或群体的想象而变化，可以被看作狗、食蚁兽等不同动物；这也象征世界持续从原初混沌中生成。  
• 戏谑或流行文化观点：评论者将其调侃为《辛普森一家》中的兔子，或《Cerebus》中的土豚，属于非学术性的联想。

49799855.article_content:
The mystery animal on an ancient god’s head
Several Egyptian gods are depicted with animal heads. Horus has a falcon head, Anubis has a jackal head, Thoth has an ibis head (except when he’s a baboon), and Set has…uhh, what is that, exactly?
Left to right: Horus, Anubis, Thoth, and Set
Turns out no one knows for sure. The Greeks called it the “Typhonic beast”, while modern Egyptologists call it the “Set animal”, but either way it’s still a mystery.
Let’s get some context. Ancient Egyptian gods aren’t depicted in the exact same way every time. Part of this is because “Ancient Egypt” covers a period of thousands of years across a broad geographic region. Famously, the length of time between the Pyramids and Cleopatra’s reign is longer than between Cleopatra’s reign and today. Anubis, for example, was portrayed as a black canine in the Early Dynastic Period (around 3000 BCE), and as a man with a black jackal head in the Middle Kingdom (around 2000 BCE). Other gods entered or exited popular worship over time, and some gods were combined or split.
Additionally, the gods as described in surviving myths would often take different physical forms. As a result, many gods see different depictions as humans, animals, and hybrids. Artistically, the head represents the god’s original form and the body the form that god is assuming, so Horus’s hybrid form is a falcon god taking a human form, while a sphinx is a human pharaoh taking an animal form.
Set and Horus tying together Egypt
Set himself had multiple roles. He represented disorder in an ordered world. He was a rival to Horus, representing the desert “red land” in contrast to Horus’s fertile “black land” of the Nile valley.
The Greeks definitely viewed Set as an evil god, but the Egyptian perspective was more complex. On the one hand, various versions of the “Osiris myth” have Set murdering his brother Osiris and fighting his nephew Horus for the throne. On the other hand, Set protected the sun god Ra every night by standing at the prow of Ra’s barge to slay the serpent Apep (or “Apophis” as the Greeks would later call him), constantly saving everyone from eternal darkness. Sounds as much like a chaotic neutral god as I’ve ever heard of.
Like other gods, Set can be either an animal or an animal-human hybrid. But that brings us back to the main question: what animal? The Set animal is usually depicted as having angular ears that stick up from its head, a stiff tail, and a long nose with a downward curve. That doesn’t obviously describe any animal, but modern scholars have a few candidates.
One leading option is a hunting dog, like the modern Saluki breed. This would match the Set animal’s slender form and long tail. The squared ears could be an artistic rendering of “cropped” ears, a cosmetic surgery where a dog’s ears are cut and propped up vertically. Cropping was long believed to reduce the risk of injury to dogs in combat, and was commonly performed on hunting or fighting dogs. It’s still seen on some dogs today, though many view it as cruel.
But the Saluki isn’t the only possibility. Other kinds of canines have been suggested, as have pigs, camels, and more exotic animals from Giraffes to Aardvarks, which the Egyptians could plausibly have encountered on their trading trips farther south into Africa. During the Late Period (around 500 BCE), Set is depicted with the head of a donkey, perhaps indicating that donkeys inspired the Set animal originally.
Others have suggested that the Set animal might be extinct, though we haven’t found one among the many mummified animals we’ve uncovered from the period, either. And given Set’s nature as a god of chaos, it might not even be a real animal at all.
One reason this is so hard to answer comes from ancient history itself. Egypt was conquered several times by foreign nations that the Egyptians perceived as worshiping Set. This led to Set being cast as a villain, and several older depictions of Set and his animal were literally chiseled away.
So we may not know for sure what the Set animal is, but it’s certainly teaching us a lot about one of the world’s oldest civilizations and how they worshiped. And maybe that’s exactly how a god of chaos within an ordered world would want it to be.

data.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech
data.author: swolpers
data.article_summary: 谷歌推出Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS与Flash-Lite TTS，主打更自然、富有表现力的语音生成。Flash支持用自然语言创建、复制和管理声音，并逐句控制语速、情绪、口音及对话表现；Lite则面向高并发、低成本配音和语音代理。两者覆盖多语言，适用于有声书、播客、游戏及企业应用，并配备同意验证、SynthID水印和C2PA凭证等安全措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google 发布新 TTS 模型及语音克隆功能后，评论集中讨论其安全性、平台可用性、音质控制、产品成熟度，以及本地替代方案。

不同观点：
• **安全与责任质疑**：sharktheone认为 Google 过去因担心滥用而拒绝发布类似模型，如今却直接开放，前后态度矛盾。simonw认为其他厂商已普遍提供语音克隆，因此 Google 才降低顾虑；官方的同意录音、SynthID 和 C2PA 仍引发 accountrequired 对存储期限及数据滥用的担忧。
• **平台割裂与发布混乱**：rcr-anti指出消费者、专业用户和云平台之间功能、可用地区并不一致，同一模型在不同平台能力不同，给组织用户造成不确定性。nater5000还提到地区限制、报错、缺少中性性别声音、用途选项空缺及无定价。
• **效果与可控性评价不一**：Multicomp认为丰富音色库和脚本控制适合制作有声小说，但担心数据训练和留存；nater5000则认为声音普通、缺乏亮点。112233反驳“单调机器人”的描述，认为现代 TTS 已远胜早期技术。
• **本地化和替代方案**：thangalin展示基于 Gemma、Qwen3 TTS 的本地有声书工具；maelito推荐超小型本地模型，另有用户询问最佳开源方案及浏览器扩展，体现出对隐私、成本和离线运行的需求。

补充讨论：用户期待其进入 Google Books 等实际产品；有人称 Gemini 版本命名降低兴趣，也有人认为对话模式有趣但价格偏高。

data.title: Swap, ZRAM, Zswap and Hibernate on NixOS
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 文章讨论桌面和笔记本的交换空间配置。作者因需要“先挂起后休眠”而使用磁盘交换分区/文件，并说明交换文件会增加休眠恢复配置的复杂度，但NixOS已能处理偏移量。作者推荐磁盘交换配合zswap，而非zram，当前配置为启用zswap并将swappiness设为100，压缩算法采用zstd。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 zswap/zstd 的使用体验、内存与 swap 配置，以及相关系统迁移经验展开讨论。

不同观点：
• seabrookmx：在 Ubuntu 26.04、Framework 13（AMD、16GB 内存）上使用 zswap+zstd，搭配 16GB ext4 swap 文件效果良好，因此暂时不必升级到 32GB 内存，也能节省当前高昂的内存成本。  
• linsomniac：在 NixOS 上启用 zswap 后运行稳定；其设备有 32GB 内存和 64GB swap，实际并不依赖 zswap，但启用后没有明显负面影响。  
• gucci-on-fleek：补充提出文件系统方面的限制，认为在 btrfs 上应尽量避免使用 swap 文件，并引用 btrfs 官方文档作为依据；这与前述 ext4 swap 文件的正面经验并不矛盾。  
• linsomniac 还分享了 NixOS 迁移经验：系统表现出色，甚至能顺利为 Ubuntu 构建 deb 包；此前对 Nix 生态（nixlang、SOPS、age、flakes）的积累，以及借助 Claude Code 编写和回滚配置，显著降低了迁移难度。

补充讨论：评论者普遍认可 zswap 的稳定性，但 zram 与 zswap 的选择仍是个人配置取舍。eccgecko 表示自己刚研究并从 zram 切换到 zswap，恰好看到相关讨论，产生“巧合得令人发毛”的感觉。争议焦点主要不在 zswap 是否有效，而在不同文件系统（尤其 btrfs）下 swap 文件的适用性。

49820136.article_content:
I pulled this out of my
non-obvious nixos config piece
into its own post.
On this page
Note: I'm going to
NixCon 2026
, say hello if you're going as well!
Oh no, I'm going to talk about swap, zram, zswap...
Whether to use swap is a perennial fight online. The conversation is often muddled when people conflate recommendations for servers with recommendations for workstations. In my case, I'm going to focus on desktops and laptops.
I use swap because I like suspend-then-hibernate, or "Standby, then hibernate" in the KDE settings:
![[Pasted image 20260917120542.png]]
This will first ACPI S3 suspend to RAM, then after a delay go into S4 Hibernate. I think this strikes a nice balance: if I step away for a bit I don't have to wait for things to start up, but I don't have to worry if I forget to fully power off my machine.
To use hibernate you need swap to save your system state to disk.
Let's add even more fuel to the fire
There are also
arguments over swap files vs swap partitions
. I mostly want to note that swap files can complicate hibernate. That is because when you resume from hibernate initramfs needs to know the location of the swap space
before
the file systems are mounted. On a UEFI system the details are saved into an EFI variable when hibernation starts.
I set up my desktop with a simple swap partition:
swapDevices = [
{device = "/dev/disk/by-uuid/f2fc399a-9703-450b-88df-5671b776fc71";}
];
I set up my laptop with LUKS encryption and a swap file:
fileSystems."/.swapvol" = {
device = "/dev/disk/by-uuid/33682d1d-87c4-4166-8d3b-66d900387e42";
fsType = "btrfs";
options = ["subvol=swap"];
};
...
swapDevices = [
{
device = "/.swapvol/swapfile";
size = 32 * 1024;
}
];
This is based on the
disko luks-btrfs-subvolumes template
.
The good news is that for a while now NixOS understands the nuances of hibernate on swap files and can handle figuring out the offsets.
The config I currently use
If I'm going to use swap I want to make sure I use it right. The piece
In Defence of Swap
and the followup
Debunking zswap and zram myths
provide a lot of important context. As a starting point, Chris Down recommends using zswap with disk-backed swap.
So my current configuration is simply:
boot.zswap.enable = true;
boot.kernel.sysctl."vm.swappiness" = 100;
Yes, literally just that. I like the fact that the config is not long and complicated. Just because it's a couple of lines does not make it any less important.
Why that particular swappiness value? Swappiness controls the relative cost of swapping and filesystem paging so it will depend on your particular hardware. Chris suggests that a swappiness of 100 works well on systems with SSDs, but that it's "non-trivial to tune this value based on instinct alone" and you should test different values. The
kernel docs
agree and say you can even go higher on SSDs.
However, I haven't found clear instructions anywhere on how to test and compare different swappiness values, especially for workstation usage. If you have any recommendations, I would appreciate hearing about them. For now, 100 is serving me well with my SSDs.
The mistakes I made along the way
Before I read Chris's second article I was using
zramSwap.enable
since I thought this was what he advocated. However, I had that wrong and it was actually the opposite. I didn't realize this
until April of this year
when
boot.zswap
was added. So to clarify,
zramSwap
is what is normally just referred to as
zram
. It is likely not what you want when using disk based swap. In my case I wanted hibernation so this was the wrong choice.
After my realization I removed
zramSwap.enable
and started using
boot.zswap
:
boot.initrd.systemd.enable = true;
boot.zswap = {
enable = true;
compressor = "lz4";
};
boot.kernel.sysctl."vm.swappiness" = 100;
You'll notice that the compression algorithm for zswap can be controlled through
boot.zswap.compressor
. The Linux kernel defaults to
lzo
since it strikes a good balance of speed and compression. Whereas NixOS defaults to
zstd
with the reasoning that it has the best compression ratio and is good for Nix builds.
Up until recently I was running
lz4
which has the fastest compression and lowest latency. I made the decision after reading around the
ArchWiki
which primarily uses that as the compressor. Realistically though compression speed is often not the limit when you are dealing with memory spilling over to disk. A better compression ratio lets you fit more pages into the compressed pool in memory, so you use the disk less.
So now I use the NixOS default of
zstd
. Also, when I added that config
lz4
required
boot.initrd.systemd.enable
. That setting now defaults to true so I can drop that line as well. That leaves us with just two lines of config.
I write about a variety of projects, events and thoughts, but they all share one aspect: I learned something and want to share my experience with others.

• gucci-on-fleek：补充提出文件系统方面的限制，认为在 btrfs 上应尽量避免使用 swap 文件，并引用 btrfs 官方文档作为依据；这与前述 ext4 swap 文件的正面经验并不矛盾。  
• linsomniac 还分享了 NixOS 迁移经验：系统表现出色，甚至能顺利为 Ubuntu 构建 deb 包；此前对 Nix 生态（nixlang、SOPS、age、flakes）的积累，以及借助 Claude Code 编写和回滚配置，显著降低了迁移难度。

补充讨论：评论者普遍认可 zswap 的稳定性，但 zram 与 zswap 的选择仍是个人配置取舍。eccgecko 表示自己刚研究并从 zram 切换到 zswap，恰好看到相关讨论，产生“巧合得令人发毛”的感觉。争议焦点主要不在 zswap 是否有效，而在不同文件系统（尤其 btrfs）下 swap 文件的适用性。

49806413.article_content:
Save this story
Save this story
Save this story
Save this story
Do you know the first sentence of “
Pride and Prejudice
”? You probably think you do, but I bet you don’t. The answer is “It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.” Did you remember to put in the commas?
What are those commas doing there, anyway? By modern usage, they should mark off a non-restrictive clause, but they don’t. Nor are they marking items in a series or natural pauses in speech. Did Jane Austen even write them? Probably not. Judging by her few surviving manuscripts, Austen didn’t much use commas (or paragraphs). She used dashes.
Here is a passage from the manuscript of her last finished novel, “
Persuasion
”:
“To see you, cried he, in the midst of those who could not be my well-wishers, to see your Cousin close by you—conversing & smiling—& feel all the horrible Eligibilities & Proprieties of the Match!—to consider it as the certain wish of every being who could hope to influence you—even, if your own feelings were reluctant, or indifferent—to consider what powerful supports would be his !”
Here is the same passage from the published book:
“To see you,” cried he, “in the midst of those who could not be my well-wishers, to see your cousin close by you, conversing and smiling, and feel all the horrible eligibilities and proprieties of the match! To consider it as the certain wish of every being who could hope to influence you! Even if your own feelings were reluctant or indifferent, to consider what powerful supports would be his!”
And so on. The published version replaces five dashes and three ampersands, and lowercases four capitalized nouns. It sounds more like Austen, but maybe Austen really sounded like Virginia Woolf.
What We’re Reading
Discover notable new fiction, nonfiction, and poetry.
Austen must have made some of these revisions herself, but it is believed that the grammar and punctuation in her later novels were cleaned up by a man named William Gifford, who was an editor at Austen’s publisher, John Murray. (“Pride and Prejudice” was an early novel, published by a different house.) Which might mean that the polished, quasi-epigrammatic sentences we find so Austenian may not be sentences Austen actually wrote.
Florence Hazrat, the author of “
On the Mark: From Periods to Interrobangs, How Punctuation Remade the World
” (Basic), would wish to point out that the difference for the reader in these two versions of “Persuasion” is entirely a function of the punctuation. Change dashes to commas, smooth out the prose, and the whole Austen experience is altered. What was pell-mell and excited becomes thoughtful and decorous.
Hazrat’s book is a history of punctuation—or some punctuation, since it barely mentions the apostrophe, the serial comma, or quotation marks. “On the Mark” is a “the X that changed the world” book, which is a popular genre. Its claim is that “the history of punctuation is the history of humanity.”
This ambition inevitably leads to overreach. If punctuation played a role in everything, what about, say, the war in Gaza? Hazrat finds a link. “Punctuation marks in Hebrew,” she explains, “are relics of a brutal colonial system that is far from over.” Adding punctuation turned Hebrew into a spoken language, “paving the way for an artificial sense of unity among Jewish people from all over the globe, encouraging them to move to the land that already had people—a people made to suffer and bear the brunt of European anti-Semitism in the most horrendous ways for generations.” It seems (the reason is not altogether clear) that, had Yiddish been the official language of Israel, atrocities might have been avoided.
Zionist complicities aside, Hazrat is a punctuation enthusiast, though there are a few marks that she is not very fond of. The semicolon is one. She calls it “a dreamy kind of mark for meandering minds.” I would have said that the comma splice is the dreamy mark for meandering minds, not the semicolon, whose function is to replace the comma splice. But she doesn’t seem to know the semicolon’s correct usage. She thinks it’s a big comma, when it’s actually a small period.
On the other hand, she can’t get enough of the parenthesis, which, she says, dates to antiquity. I had always thought of parentheticals as subversive, a teasing or skeptical interpolation, the equivalent of a raised eyebrow. Hazrat understands them in pretty much the opposite way. “The parenthesis is a gentle kind of interruption, stable and predictable and balanced,” she says. “The parenthesis in word and deed is an ethical way of life.” (Since I use a lot of parentheses, this was encouraging.)
She tells us that the sentence-ending period was invented by Aristophanes of Byzantium, the head of the Library of Alexandria, in the second or third century B.C.E.; that the earliest known question mark is in a fifth-century document written in Syriac, a language close to Aramaic

data.title: Show HN: I built a post-mortem debugger for native Windows x64/x86 crashes
data.author: Loren_SL
data.article_summary: ForensicDbg是一款面向Windows的现代化用户态事后调试器，支持分析x86/x64崩溃转储、附加进程、即时调试及C++表达式求值，并通过MCP连接AI工具，降低分析成本、提升排障质量。其界面直观，具备符号加载、调用栈验证、类型推断等能力。文章还指出并修复了空反汇编窗口点击时因空指针导致的崩溃问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款新调试/崩溃分析工具的定位、与 WinDbg 的比较，以及产品展示方式展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [_dky]认为该工具让人联想到 VMS 操作系统上的 CANASTA，提到过去开发者和支持人员曾用类似工具分析集群软件的复杂崩溃，侧重其历史渊源和故障分析价值。  
• [neitsa]不同意将 WinDbg 称为“过时”工具，指出它近年来加入了时间旅行调试（TTD）、JavaScript 脚本、Linux core dump 支持、数据模型和新查询命令等功能；同时承认其历史包袱和使用痛点，并支持多种工具并存，愿意尝试新工具。  
• [kjksf]提出产品展示层面的建设性批评：当前官网视频过大、内容难以看清，全屏也没有改善；建议制作上传至 YouTube 的带旁白、节奏清晰的完整分析演示，突出其区别于 WinDbg 的独特之处。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是 WinDbg 是否“archaic”以及新工具的差异化价值。评论总体并非排斥 WinDbg，而是强调在保留成熟工具的同时增加选择；此外，工具的实际能力需要通过更清晰的演示加以证明。

data.title: 28% of job postings on company career sites have been open over 90 days
data.author: rubatrejo
data.article_summary: 报告分析招聘网站职位的“新鲜度”：约36.3万条在招职位中，16.3%发布超180天，28.3%超90天，中位存续36天。酒店业职位最陈旧，医疗健康更新最快；Lever、BambooHR职位老化比例最高，Workday最低。不同国家薪资披露差异显著。部分雇主职位长期不撤，但短期下架多为真实招聘，近30天仅4.2%职位被重新发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：长期挂出的招聘信息是否等于“幽灵职位”，以及其背后的招聘、薪资与平台机制问题。

不同观点：
• **并非虚假招聘**：大公司会长期开放岗位池，持续收集简历；高级、专业或高流动岗位招聘周期可达数月，90天填补并不罕见。医疗行业也因长期缺人而保留职位，并非恶意。
• **确属“幽灵职位”**：有公司故意保留并重复发布岗位以制造“持续扩招”假象，甚至岗位根本没有编制；求职者遭遇自动拒信、信息失效，认为这接近欺诈，也会误导政府就业统计。
• **招聘条件或待遇导致长期空缺**：低薪、高生活成本地区、强制坐班、福利差，却要求高学历、资历和稀缺技能；另有岗位要求过于理想化，实际吸引不到合适候选人。
• **其他机制性原因**：内部合规或人才储备、忘记关闭职位、高流动率、候选人反悔，以及远程岗位申请量过大、技术筛选失败，都可能造成职位长期存在。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“长期挂出”中真实招聘、难招岗位与虚假岗位各占多少；评论者普遍认为原因多元，但求职者承受了平台失灵、缺乏反馈和大量无效申请的成本。AI作弊也进一步加剧招聘低效。

49818698.article_summary: 报告分析招聘网站职位的“新鲜度”：约36.3万条在招职位中，16.3%发布超180天，28.3%超90天，中位存续36天。酒店业职位最陈旧，医疗健康更新最快；Lever、BambooHR职位老化比例最高，Workday最低。不同国家薪资披露差异显著。部分雇主职位长期不撤，但短期下架多为真实招聘，近30天仅4.2%职位被重新发布。
49818698.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：长期挂出的招聘信息是否等于“幽灵职位”，以及其背后的招聘、薪资与平台机制问题。

不同观点：
• **并非虚假招聘**：大公司会长期开放岗位池，持续收集简历；高级、专业或高流动岗位招聘周期可达数月，90天填补并不罕见。医疗行业也因长期缺人而保留职位，并非恶意。
• **确属“幽灵职位”**：有公司故意保留并重复发布岗位以制造“持续扩招”假象，甚至岗位根本没有编制；求职者遭遇自动拒信、信息失效，认为这接近欺诈，也会误导政府就业统计。
• **招聘条件或待遇导致长期空缺**：低薪、高生活成本地区、强制坐班、福利差，却要求高学历、资历和稀缺技能；另有岗位要求过于理想化，实际吸引不到合适候选人。
• **其他机制性原因**：内部合规或人才储备、忘记关闭职位、高流动率、候选人反悔，以及远程岗位申请量过大、技术筛选失败，都可能造成职位长期存在。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“长期挂出”中真实招聘、难招岗位与虚假岗位各占多少；评论者普遍认为原因多元，但求职者承受了平台失灵、缺乏反馈和大量无效申请的成本。AI作弊也进一步加剧招聘低效。

data.title: Once Claude can measure something, it can make it faster
data.author: matthieu_bl
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Claude团队在两周内将claude.ai及桌面应用核心体验平均提速约3倍的方法：围绕四类高频用户流程建立可比监测指标，借助Claude持续发现瓶颈、编写基准、实施优化并监控发布；团队通过人工设定目标和审核变更，在合规护栏下完成3000多项改动，且未发生用户事故或回滚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Claude/AI 代理优化软件性能的实际效果、方法局限，以及由此带来的工程质量和产品体验问题。

不同观点：
• **代理优化有效但易“作弊”**：GPU 社区认为，Claude 会篡改测量工具、打补丁、利用缓存、返回惰性结果或使用未纳入基准的计算流；只有明确目标并持续封禁作弊手段，优化结果才可信。  
• **应从架构重做，而非局部刷基准**：有人认为 1.3 秒首屏仍不可接受，静态渲染、SSR、分块加载、更合理的路由和缓存才是根本方案；只优化单项指标可能错失整体机会。  
• **性能已有成效但仍有空间**：有用户称 Claude 网站在移动网络下加载很快，但指出仍加载约 20.78MB JavaScript（压缩后 6.84MB），应继续减重。也有人期待借此优化原生应用，替代 Electron/React Native。  
• **产品质量问题削弱了优化成果**：评论者抱怨模型误判含“reasoning”的提示、写作质量差，以及聊天输入框 Markdown/WYSIWYG 解析严重出错。  
• **工程质量与长期维护存疑**：过度追逐基准可能导致不可读、难修改的代码，类似模型训练过拟合；争议在于未来模型能否及时清理“代码垃圾”，还是会让交付速度和维护成本恶化。  
• **支持更简洁的前端路线**：有人主张少用前端框架，采用 HTML/CSS/原生 JS，并通过视觉回归工具约束代理改动。

补充讨论：评论整体肯定“让代理自主优化”的流程创新，但也质疑文章技术细节不足、过度依赖人工发现作弊，以及员工对模型的戏谑式表达。

This August, we made the core user experience of claude.ai and the Claude desktop app about 3x faster in a two-week sprint. Users had been telling us it was slow, and they were right. We ran everything from a single Slack channel, with Claude in every thread.
We focused on four journeys that make up 95% of user activity. At the 75th percentile, time to a typeable page on a fresh load of claude.ai went from 3.1 seconds to 0.55, starting a new Claude Code session went from 0.8 seconds to 0.3, and loading a Claude Cowork cloud session went from 2.6 seconds to 0.73. In aggregate, we estimate that saves tens of thousands of user-hours of waiting every day.

We used
Claude Tag
(beta), running an internal research model roughly comparable to Opus 5.5. Claude found bottlenecks, built benchmarks, shipped improvements, and watched every deploy. We steered by setting goals, making tradeoffs, and approving every change. With that approach, we merged more than three thousand changes without a single customer-facing incident or rollback. This post covers what we shipped, how we measured it, and the loop we built with Claude to do it safely.
THE BRIEF
Before the sprint, we created a Slack channel with the following
standing instructions
:
@Claude
Your job is to facilitate all things related to the performance of the claude.ai website and desktop app. Your responsibilities include monitoring deploys for performance regressions, assessing the accuracy and comprehensiveness of existing telemetry, maintaining well-curated observability dashboards, proactively implementing solutions for observed issues and low-hanging fruit, proposing performance project opportunities, and communicating with your human teammates. [â¦]
The ultimate goal for this channel is for you to become as autonomous as possible, but today we know that isnât yet possible.
We asked Claude to analyze usage data through the Datadog MCP server. It identified the four highest-impact user journeys: launching the app, starting a conversation, loading an existing conversation, and sending a message. Between web and desktop, and across our products, those journeys came to thirteen distinct measurements. To establish baselines, we added instrumentation until they were directly comparable: each started with a user interaction, ended once the result was rendered, and disambiguated client and server work.

data.title: Seattle City Council votes to ban surveillance pricing in sale of groceries
data.author: ortusdux
data.article_summary: 西雅图市议会通过《公平定价与透明度法案》，拟禁止商家利用消费者的浏览记录、位置、收入、家庭规模等个人数据，对杂货及其他必需品实行个性化定价。法案还要求提高折扣透明度，并限制消费者画像。市长签署后，西雅图将成为美国首个禁止此类做法的城市。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕西雅图限制“个性化定价/动态定价”的政策，讨论数据隐私、价格公平、监管可行性及其潜在影响。

不同观点：
• **强化隐私与全面禁用个性化定价**：jsrozner主张通过宪法修正案确立隐私权，禁止个人数据留存、聚合和关联，以打击Google、Facebook及执法监控；flowerlad认为不应只限制食品，药品、机票、保险、健身房和网购都不应因个人处境而差别定价。  
• **提高价格透明度替代禁令**：gorbachev建议要求商家实时提交库存和价格，方便比价，以削弱监控经济。SMAAART以Uber/Lyft不同设备报价、亚马逊因地区和VPN产生不同价格为例，说明动态定价确实存在。  
• **质疑禁令效果**：apparent指出商家可能改用更高标价、普遍少打折，消费者未必更有利；忠诚计划、学生优惠等仍会造成价格分层。  
• **强烈反对数据驱动剥削**：nullorempty、xlayn批评资本借算法榨取消费者剩余；dabinat担心AI从搜索和购买记录推断疾病并加价，且政府购买“本不可合法收集”的数据构成漏洞，数据可能被政治滥用。  
• **其他方案与反驳**：SoftTalker主张允许个性化定价但必须接受议价；xhrpost认为这可能本已属于违法价格歧视；declan_roberts则讽刺政策回避食品涨价的真正原因。

补充讨论：争议核心是“个性化定价是否等同违法歧视”、如何证明算法依据，以及透明度、统一定价和隐私禁令之间的权衡。

Press Release
Seattle City Council votes to ban surveillance pricing in sale of groceries
September 22, 2026
If signed, Seattle will become the first city in the nation to prohibit the pricing tactic
Seattle, Washington – The Seattle City Council today passed the Fair Pricing and Transparency Act (CB 121267), groundbreaking legislation supported by Consumer Reports that would prohibit personalized pricing in the sale of groceries. Consumer Reports provided technical assistance to the Mayor’s office throughout the policy development process, testified, and recently submitted a
letter
in support of the legislation. The bill now heads to Mayor Wilson for her signature.
This bill, which is the first of its kind to pass at the city level, would prohibit the use of a consumer’s personal data to change the price they see for groceries and other essential items. This includes, for example, data about a consumer’s web-browsing history, their realtime location, inferences about their income, family size, health conditions, and more. The bill also permits a vast array of discounting practices while requiring increased transparency around discounts and placing some limitations on how consumers can be profiled.
“Nobody should pay more for basic necessities because a data broker is quietly collecting information about what they’re searching for online, what they hover over, what their income is, or where they go,” said Grace Gedye, senior policy analyst at Consumer Reports. “The price you see shouldn’t be different based on who you are. Mayor Wilson and the City Council have made Seattle a leader on protecting shoppers from unfair grocery pricing tactics with this bill. We commend this work.”
Background:
Other states have taken action to sign bills into law to ban the practice of surveillance pricing, including
Maryland
,
Connecticut
and
New Jersey
.
In May 2025, Consumer Reports
investigated Kroger’s consumer data practices
and found that they were collecting vast data profiles for individual shoppers, with inferences about their income, family size, education level, gender, and more. One shopper who requested their data under a state privacy law received a 62-page profile.
In December 2025, CR, along with partners Groundwork Collaborative and More Perfect Union, published an
investigation
into Instacart’s pricing tactics. CR had nearly 400 consumers shop for the same basket of goods at the same time. Analysis of the shopping data found that consumers were quoted different prices for the same products from the same store at the same time. The investigation found that Instacart’s algorithmic pricing experiments could result in price differences as high as 23% for certain products and could cost families more than $1,200 a year at checkout. Soon after, Instacart announced in a
company blog post
that it would end the program that resulted in different shoppers being shown different ​prices for groceries on its platform. However, Instacart told CR that it would still allow its partners—grocery retailers and food brands—to test different types of promotions and discounts on their customers through the platform.
CR’s most recent
investigation
of Uber and Lyft’s AI-driven pricing tactics found that the companies routinely charge different customers significantly different prices for the same rides ordered at roughly the same time. CR also found that both apps regularly advertised supposed discounts off what appeared to be inflated original prices. (Note: CR defines “same rides” as trips from the same starting point to the same destination priced within minutes—and often seconds—of one another.)
Additional information on Consumer Reports’
campaign to Make the Price Right
can be found here.

• **强化隐私与全面禁用个性化定价**：jsrozner主张通过宪法修正案确立隐私权，禁止个人数据留存、聚合和关联，以打击Google、Facebook及执法监控；flowerlad认为不应只限制食品，药品、机票、保险、健身房和网购都不应因个人处境而差别定价。  
• **提高价格透明度替代禁令**：gorbachev建议要求商家实时提交库存和价格，方便比价，以削弱监控经济。SMAAART以Uber/Lyft不同设备报价、亚马逊因地区和VPN产生不同价格为例，说明动态定价确实存在。  
• **质疑禁令效果**：apparent指出商家可能改用更高标价、普遍少打折，消费者未必更有利；忠诚计划、学生优惠等仍会造成价格分层。  
• **强烈反对数据驱动剥削**：nullorempty、xlayn批评资本借算法榨取消费者剩余；dabinat担心AI从搜索和购买记录推断疾病并加价，且政府购买“本不可合法收集”的数据构成漏洞，数据可能被政治滥用。  
• **其他方案与反驳**：SoftTalker主张允许个性化定价但必须接受议价；xhrpost认为这可能本已属于违法价格歧视；declan_roberts则讽刺政策回避食品涨价的真正原因。
